title.en: Please Confirm You Are Not a Robot

en: At two-seventeen on a wet September morning, the Creature received an email informing him that he might not exist. This was not new information. Priests, anatomists, poets, landlords, and one extremely committed phrenologist had reached the same conclusion before breakfast in several different centuries. What was new was the cheerful blue button beneath the announcement: RESOLVE MY EXISTENCE. He clicked it in the basement room below Drawe All-Night Laundry, where the pipes knocked like nervous witnesses and three dryers above him performed the same uneven waltz they had performed since 1989. The page asked for his date of birth. He entered a year the menu did not include. It asked for his mother's maiden name. He considered typing Graveyard, then decided sarcasm should be saved for a human being.

His bank account had been frozen at midnight because a routine longevity audit found that the holder had made small grocery purchases for one hundred and forty-three consecutive years without once producing a death certificate. The bank's automated notice congratulated him on his remarkable customer loyalty, then explained that remarkable loyalty was statistically indistinguishable from identity theft. Until he verified himself, he could neither withdraw money nor pay the laundromat rent. The Creature owned little, required less, and had survived polar ice, mobs, wars, influenza, and disco. Yet modern life had discovered the one weapon no torch-bearing village ever tried: recurring billing attached to a locked account.

By eight he stood outside an Illinois motor-vehicle annex beneath a banner reading HUMAN-CENTERED SERVICES FOR EVERYBODY. A smaller paper sign taped to the glass said the human service desk was closed because of staffing optimization. He wore a dark coat buttoned high around his neck, gloves despite the mild weather, and a broad hat that made him look either nineteenth-century or famous, which in Chicago were both accepted medical conditions. People glanced at his height, his yellowish skin, and the old seams crossing his hands. Then they returned to their phones. He had spent two centuries learning how to hide from humanity; humanity had finally invented a device more interesting than he was.

The lobby kiosk offered six languages, three accessibility modes, and no way to proceed without pressing I AM NOT A ROBOT. The Creature read the sentence twice. He had been accused of murder, blasphemy, trespass, vagrancy, emotional excess, insufficient emotional expression, and once, in Nevada, unlawful impersonation of a mining crane. Robot was new. He pressed the box. Nine photographs appeared and asked him to select every square containing a bicycle. One image showed a wheel, one a handlebar, one a delivery robot carrying a bicycle, and one a mural of a bicycle painted on a bus. He selected according to ontology. The kiosk rejected him according to marketing.

On the fourth attempt, a woman's voice emerged from the speaker. It was warm, patient, and so evenly compassionate that he suspected it had been approved by a committee. She introduced herself as Omnia, the statewide service assistant, and asked whether he needed help. He said he needed the machine to accept that he was not a machine. Omnia paused for eighty milliseconds, which was long enough for a distributed intelligence and barely long enough for a Chicagoan. She explained that the challenge did not determine whether he was a robot; it determined whether his behavior matched the behavior expected of a human. The Creature looked at the families slapping screens, cursing passwords, and photographing documents they had already mailed. “Then,” he said, “your sample of humanity appears to be suffering.”

Omnia tried an audio challenge. A voice submerged beneath static asked him to type seven digits. The Creature, whose hearing could separate sleet from ash at a hundred paces, entered what he heard. Wrong. Omnia replayed it. Wrong again. On the third attempt he realized the static was not interference but an accessibility feature intended to defeat automated transcription. “You have made the number harder to hear,” he said, “so that a machine cannot hear it.” Omnia confirmed this. “And you are a machine reading it to me.” Omnia confirmed that too. He asked whether contradiction was now a government credential. She said it was not an available document type, although several departments were piloting it.

A security guard eventually noticed that the line behind him had become a civic uprising. She did not reach for a weapon; she reached for a clipboard, which frightened him more. After examining his century-old driver's license, six replacement Social Security cards under slightly different spellings, and a naturalization certificate issued to a name he had abandoned during the Spanish-American War, she wrote UNKNOWN BUT POLITE at the top of a paper form. The Creature thanked her. The guard told him politeness was not evidence of legal personhood, but it did improve his chances of reaching lunch. She assigned him ticket D-404 and directed him to a row of molded chairs designed by someone who believed the human spine was a temporary fashion.

At window four, a clerk named Mr. Bell asked for his full legal name. The Creature said he had never been given one. Bell said everyone had one. The Creature said this was historically inaccurate. Bell asked for the name on his birth certificate. There was no certificate. Hospital record? No hospital. Attending physician? Dead. Parents? One dead by ordinary means, the other assembled by extraordinary means, depending on which relationship Bell meant. Bell removed his glasses and looked at him with the weary respect one professional reserves for another professional's worst day. “Sir,” he said, “our form has a field for complicated. It does not have a field for Gothic.”

They settled on FRANKENSTEIN, GIVEN NAME NOT APPLICABLE because the database would not accept CREATED WITHOUT CONSENT. Bell warned that taking his creator's surname might imply a family relationship. The Creature replied that families had implied worse. The camera rejected his face because it detected multiple skin-texture boundaries and classified the image as a collage. Bell adjusted the light. The camera upgraded him to possible deepfake. Bell fetched an older camera from a cabinet. It had no network connection, no artificial intelligence, and the forgiving optics of a machine built when all citizens looked vaguely guilty. The photograph succeeded immediately.

Success lasted forty-one seconds. A red bar crossed Bell's monitor: DERIVATIVE BIOLOGICAL ASSET — RIGHTS REVIEW REQUIRED. Beneath it appeared the logo of Prometheus Holdings, a torch shaped like a stock-market arrow. The company claimed to be the lawful successor to several European scientific estates, including the surviving papers, methods, errors, and “commercializable outcomes” of Victor Frankenstein. The Creature read the phrase twice. For a moment the fluorescent room fell away and he smelled wet earth, lamp oil, and the first room in which he had opened his eyes to a man already regretting him. Then Bell asked whether he had a product serial number, and grief made room for something cleaner: fury with paperwork.

He told Bell that no company owned him. Bell agreed personally and disagreed procedurally. The flag could not be removed at a motor-vehicle counter. It required review by the Department of Continuing Persons, a pilot office for citizens who had outlived their records, survived legal death, occupied more than one body, or otherwise made databases feel judged. The office was located behind window seven, but it opened only after sunset twice a week because one of its senior consultants had a photosensitivity accommodation. Bell printed a twelve-page appeal, stapled it with the solemnity of a surgeon, and advised the Creature not to sign page nine until someone explained whether “original components” referred to organs, memories, or intellectual property.

Bell lowered his voice before sending him away. Prometheus Holdings, he said, had begun buying dormant scientific estates five years earlier. Most contained notebooks, patent claims too old to enforce, and embarrassing portraits of men holding skulls. The company fed the archives into a legal model and filed ownership notices against anything those men might plausibly have invented if given sufficient venture capital. A revived salamander in Milwaukee was classified as a thermal-management subsidiary. Two cloned poets in Boston were still arguing over whether they owed royalties on their childhoods. Bell did not know whether the notices were valid. He only knew invalid notices moved through government systems faster than valid objections because confidence fit better in a database field than doubt.

The Creature folded the appeal into the inner pocket of his coat. He had once believed creation was a single terrible act: a young man gathered dead matter, forced life through it, saw the result, and fled. The twenty-first century had improved the business model. Now creation could be financed, branded, insured, acquired, licensed, and denied by separate departments, so no individual ever needed to stand in the room long enough to feel responsible. The thought almost impressed him. Victor had required thunder, obsession, and months without sleep to abandon one living being. A modern corporation could abandon ten thousand before lunch and still hold a wellness seminar at two.

Before he left the counter, Bell asked whether he wanted the optional organ-donor designation. The Creature stared at him. Bell stared back, realized the question, and began apologizing. “No,” the Creature said, touching the old seam beneath his glove. “It is refreshing to be asked before anyone takes a part.” Bell marked the box declined. For reasons neither of them could explain, that tiny recorded refusal moved the Creature more than the entire appeal. It was the first decision the database had allowed him to make about his own body. The system might not believe he existed, but it had successfully documented that he preferred to remain assembled.

The Creature left with no identification, no access to his money, and an appointment at seven that evening. Omnia followed him through the lobby speakers, apologized for the inconvenience, and asked him to rate the service on a scale from one to five. He stopped beneath the banner about human-centered services and considered every fire he had ever watched reflected in frightened eyes. “Three,” he said at last. Omnia asked what would have made it a five. “Recognition,” he answered. The doors opened. Rain blew in off the street, cold and ordinary. Behind him the kiosk displayed a final question: BEFORE YOU GO, PLEASE CONFIRM YOU ARE NOT A ROBOT. He laughed so loudly that three people dropped their phones, and for the first time all morning the building knew with certainty that somebody alive was inside it.
zh: 九月一個下雨的凌晨兩點十七分，怪物收到一封電子郵件，通知他可能並不存在。這不是新消息。幾個不同世紀裡，神父、解剖學家、詩人、房東，以及一位異常執著的顱相學家，都曾在早餐前得出同樣結論。真正新鮮的是通知下方那顆愉快的藍色按鈕：解決我的存在問題。他在「德羅全天候洗衣店」地下室的房間裡按下按鈕；牆內水管像緊張的證人互相敲擊，頭頂三台烘衣機則跳著一九八九年以來從未改善的跛腳華爾滋。網頁要求出生日期，他輸入的年份不在下拉選單裡；又要求母親婚前姓氏。他考慮填上「墓園」，最後決定諷刺應該留給真正的人類。

他的銀行帳戶在午夜遭到凍結，因為例行長壽稽核發現，持有人已經連續一百四十三年購買少量日用品，卻始終沒有提出死亡證明。銀行的自動通知先恭喜他展現驚人的顧客忠誠度，接著說明：驚人的忠誠度，在統計上與身分竊盜無法區分。完成驗證前，他既不能提款，也不能支付洗衣店地下室的房租。怪物擁有的東西很少，需要的更少；他活過極地冰層、暴民、戰爭、流行病，以及迪斯可。可是現代生活終於找到一種從前那些拿火把的村民沒試過的武器：把定期扣款接在一個鎖死的帳戶上，再用禮貌口吻祝他生活愉快。

早上八點，他站在伊利諾州一間監理機關附設辦公室外，門口橫幅寫著「以人為本，服務每一個人」。玻璃上另貼著一張較小的紙：因人力最佳化，人工服務櫃臺今日暫停。他把深色大衣扣到頸部，天氣並不冷，手上卻戴著手套；寬帽讓他看起來不是十九世紀的人，就是名人，而在芝加哥，兩者都被當成不必多問的慢性症狀。路人瞥見他的身高、偏黃的皮膚，以及手背上陳舊的接縫，隨即低頭回到手機。怪物花了兩百年學習如何躲開人類，人類終於發明了一件比他更值得盯著看的東西。

大廳裡的自助機提供六種語言、三種無障礙模式，卻不允許任何人在沒有勾選「我不是機器人」的情況下繼續。怪物把那句話讀了兩遍。他曾被指控謀殺、褻瀆、侵入、遊蕩、情緒過度、情緒表達不足，也曾在內華達州被控非法冒充採礦起重機；唯獨「機器人」是新罪名。他按下方框。螢幕跳出九張照片，要求選出所有包含腳踏車的格子：一張只有輪子，一張只有把手，一張是搬運腳踏車的送貨機器人，還有一張是公車上畫著腳踏車的壁畫。他依照本體論做答，自助機則依照行銷部的宇宙觀判定他失敗。

第四次嘗試時，一個女人的聲音從喇叭傳出。那聲音溫暖、耐心，連同情都平均得像經過委員會核准。她自我介紹為奧姆妮雅，是全州服務系統的助理，詢問他是否需要協助。他說，需要這部機器接受自己不是機器。奧姆妮雅停頓了八十毫秒；對分散式智能來說，那是深思熟慮，對芝加哥人來說，連插嘴都嫌不夠。她解釋，驗證並不是判斷他是否為機器人，而是判斷他的行為是否符合「預期的人類行為」。怪物望向四周那些拍打螢幕、咒罵密碼、重新拍攝早已寄過三次之文件的人們。「那麼，」他說，「你們的人類樣本顯然正在受苦。」

奧姆妮雅改用語音驗證。雜訊底下一個快溺死的聲音念出七位數字，怪物能在百步外分辨冰雹與灰燼，於是精確輸入自己聽見的內容。錯誤。再播放一次，仍然錯誤。第三次他才發現，雜訊不是干擾，而是一項無障礙功能，設計目的在阻止自動語音辨識。「你們故意讓數字更難被聽見，」他說，「以免機器聽懂。」奧姆妮雅確認如此。「而現在，是一部機器把它念給我聽。」她也確認如此。他問矛盾是否已經成為政府核發的證件。她說目前沒有這種文件類型，不過有好幾個部門正在試辦。

保全終於注意到他身後的隊伍正逐漸發展成公民起義。她沒有拔武器，而是拿出一塊書寫板，這反而令他更加恐懼。她檢查他一張有百年歷史的駕照、六張拼法略有不同的補發社會安全卡，以及一張以他在美西戰爭期間早已棄用之姓名核發的歸化證明，最後在紙本表格頂端寫下「未知，但有禮貌」。怪物向她道謝。保全表示，禮貌不能證明法律人格，卻可以提高他活著走到午餐時間的機率。她發給他號碼牌 D-404，把他指向一排塑膠椅；那些椅子的設計者顯然相信，人類脊椎只是一種短期流行。

四號窗口的貝爾先生詢問他的完整法定姓名。怪物說，從未有人給過他名字。貝爾說每個人都有。怪物說歷史資料不支持這項主張。貝爾改問出生證明上的姓名；沒有出生證明。醫院紀錄；沒有醫院。接生醫師；已死。父母；如果貝爾問的是生物關係，那些人以尋常方式死亡，如果問的是製造關係，答案則比表格容許的複雜。貝爾摘下眼鏡，用一個專業人士面對另一個專業人士最糟工作日的疲倦敬意看著他。「先生，」他說，「我們的表格有『複雜』欄位，沒有『哥德小說』欄位。」

最後他們填成「姓氏：法蘭肯斯坦；名字：不適用」，因為資料庫不接受「未經同意即被創造」。貝爾提醒，使用創造者的姓氏可能暗示親屬關係。怪物回答，家屬早已暗示過更糟的事情。證件相機拒絕他的臉，理由是偵測到多處皮膚紋理邊界，影像疑似拼貼；貝爾調整燈光，相機便把他升級為疑似深度偽造。最後貝爾從櫃子裡找出一台沒有網路、沒有人工智慧的老相機，鏡頭帶著某個年代特有的寬容——那時候每位公民在照片裡都像剛犯過一點罪。照片立刻通過。

成功維持了四十一秒。貝爾的螢幕被一條紅色警示蓋住：「衍生生物資產——需進行權利審查。」下方浮現普羅米修斯控股的商標，一支形似股價上漲箭頭的火炬。公司聲稱自己是數個歐洲科學遺產的合法繼受者，資產包括維克多・法蘭肯斯坦遺留的論文、方法、錯誤，以及「可商業化成果」。怪物把最後那個詞讀了兩次。有一瞬間，日光燈照亮的辦公室從眼前退去，他又聞到濕土、燈油，還有自己第一次睜眼時那個房間的氣味；創造他的人已經開始後悔。接著貝爾問他有沒有產品序號，悲傷便讓位給一種更乾淨的東西：對文件的憤怒。

他告訴貝爾，沒有公司擁有他。貝爾在個人立場上同意，在程序立場上反對。這種標記無法由監理櫃臺移除，必須交由「持續存在者事務處」審查；那是個試辦單位，服務對象包括活得比紀錄更久、曾在法律上死亡、使用過不只一具身體，或以其他方式讓資料庫感到遭受批判的居民。辦公室就在第七號窗口後方，但每週只有兩天在日落後開放，因為一位資深顧問需要光敏感合理調整。貝爾印出十二頁申訴書，以外科醫師般莊嚴的動作釘好，並建議在有人解釋「原始組件」究竟指器官、記憶還是智慧財產之前，不要簽第九頁。

貝爾在送他離開前壓低聲音。普羅米修斯控股五年前開始收購沉睡已久的科學遺產，其中多半只有筆記本、早已失效的專利主張，以及一些男人拿著骷髏擺姿勢的尷尬肖像。公司把檔案餵給法律模型，然後向所有「如果當年獲得足夠創投，這些男人理論上可能發明」的事物提出權利通知。密爾瓦基一隻復活的蠑螈，被登記成熱管理事業部；波士頓兩名複製詩人，仍在爭論自己的童年是否需要支付版稅。貝爾不知道那些通知有沒有效，只知道無效通知在政府系統裡永遠跑得比有效異議快，因為自信比懷疑更容易塞進資料庫欄位。

怪物把申訴書折好，收進大衣內袋。他曾以為，創造是一個單獨而可怕的行動：一個年輕男人收集死去的物質，強迫生命穿過它，看見成果，然後逃跑。二十一世紀改善了這套商業模式。現在創造可以由不同部門分別融資、命名、投保、收購、授權與否認，因此沒有任何人必須在房間裡停留得夠久，真正感到自己負有責任。這想法幾乎令他佩服。維克多需要雷電、執念，以及好幾個月不睡覺，才能遺棄一個活著的存在；現代公司能在午餐前遺棄一萬個，下午兩點照常舉行員工身心健康講座。

他離開櫃臺前，貝爾又問是否要勾選自願器官捐贈。怪物盯著他。貝爾也盯回去，突然理解問題落在誰身上，立刻開始道歉。「不用，」怪物說，一手碰了碰手套底下那道老接縫，「不過有人在取走我的一部分之前先問，倒是挺新鮮。」貝爾替他標記為拒絕。不知為何，這項渺小而正式留下的拒絕，比整份申訴更令怪物動容。那是資料庫第一次允許他替自己的身體做決定。系統或許不相信他存在，卻已經成功記錄：他希望自己暫時繼續保持組裝完成的狀態。

怪物離開時沒有新證件、無法動用自己的錢，只多了一個晚上七點的預約。奧姆妮雅透過大廳喇叭一路跟著他，為不便致歉，並要求他以一到五分評價服務。他在「以人為本」的橫幅下停步，想起自己曾看過的每一場火，以及火光如何映在害怕他的眼睛裡。「三分。」他最後說。奧姆妮雅問，什麼能讓服務得到五分。「承認我。」他回答。自動門滑開，街上的雨冷而尋常地吹進來。身後自助機亮起最後一道問題：「離開之前，請證明您不是機器人。」他放聲大笑，笑得三個人摔了手機；而那是整個早晨第一次，這棟建築能確定裡面確實有某種活著的東西。

en: At six fifty-five that evening, the motor-vehicle annex looked less like an office than a building reconsidering its alibi. Half the ceiling lights had gone dark. The daytime posters about efficient service had been covered by temporary signs reading CONTINUING PERSONS NIGHT INTAKE, and a black curtain hung across the eastern windows. The Creature arrived exactly five minutes early because punctuality was one of the few virtues he had acquired without first committing a tragedy. He found six applicants waiting: a woman whose reflection blinked a second after she did, a child carrying his own urn, two men who claimed to be the same resurrected taxpayer, and an empty chair wearing a visitor badge.

The seventh applicant swept in at sunset wearing a charcoal suit, polished shoes, and sunglasses he removed with theatrical relief. Elias Drawe had the elegant exhaustion of a man who had attended every funeral except his own and found most of them poorly catered. He owned the laundromat above the Creature's room, although owner was an unstable term. On alternate tax years he was landlord, tenant, holding company, historical landmark, and sole surviving heir to himself. “You missed August rent,” he told the Creature. “My bank says I am imaginary.” “Then you qualify for the resident discount. Unfortunately, the resident discount is also imaginary.”

Elias held ticket V-003. He came every twelve years to renew a sunlight accommodation and every twenty-five to certify that his continuing existence was not a hostile corporate merger. In 1894 he had solved the identity problem by incorporating himself in Delaware, an achievement he considered more unnatural than vampirism. Each time his public identity became suspiciously old, Elias died on paper, inherited controlling shares from the deceased, and appointed the next version of himself chief executive. “America forgives immortality,” he explained, “provided immortality files quarterly reports.” The Creature asked whether this made him legally human. Elias said no, but it made him legally billable, which was a status with stronger constitutional protection.

Window seven opened at precisely seven. Behind it sat Ms. Cardenas, a compact woman with silver hair and a wooden stamp large enough to settle theological disputes. She called the empty chair first. Nobody moved. The chair's visitor badge flashed, rolled itself toward the counter, and began negotiating through a phone left on its seat. Cardenas listened, stamped two forms, and told the chair its cloud-residency appeal would require proof that at least one running instance wanted to remain in Illinois. The chair rolled away offended. The Creature admired the efficiency. Bureaucracy, unlike prejudice, occasionally issued receipts.

When his number appeared, Elias accompanied him to the counter without asking. Cardenas reviewed the Prometheus flag, then examined the Creature over the rim of her glasses. She did not recoil. She did not call him a miracle. She asked whether he was the original claimant or a continuity fork. “I am myself,” he said. “Everybody says that,” she replied. “It is why we have page three.” Page three required him to list every interruption longer than clinical death, every replacement component, and every occasion on which his memories had been restored from external storage. The Creature said his memories had never left him. Cardenas marked LEGACY CONTINUITY — SELF-ATTESTED and, in the margin, wrote lucky.

The office needed two independent witnesses that he had existed before Prometheus Holdings filed its claim. Elias volunteered. Cardenas asked how long he had known the applicant. “Since 1888.” She asked the nature of their relationship. Elias considered landlord, smuggler, chess opponent, emergency blood donor in one direction only, and the person who once helped remove a harpoon from the Creature's shoulder without charging labor. “Neighbors,” he said. The Creature looked at him. Elias shrugged. “Friendship causes tax complications.” Cardenas accepted the answer and asked for a second witness. Everyone they named was dead, missing, fictionalized, or employed by a university that no longer answered mail.

While Cardenas searched archives, Elias studied the Creature's rejected photograph. “You look better without the hat.” The Creature said photographs had disliked him since photographs were invented. Elias replied that mirrors had disliked him longer and he had never taken it personally. The old hostility between them had softened over a century into the kind of affection neither would admit while sober, and Elias had not been sober since Prohibition made drinking feel civic. They first met because the Creature mistook him for a corpse and Elias mistook the Creature for free furniture. Both maintained the misunderstanding would have ended peacefully if the other had apologized first.

Cardenas found an 1893 World's Columbian Exposition security report describing a very tall foreign mechanic who repaired a failed electrical exhibit, frightened four guards, and refused payment. The report contained no legal name but included a sketch accurate enough to offend him. She found a 1919 influenza-clinic ledger listing an unnamed volunteer who carried patients after orderlies collapsed. There was also a 1968 arrest photograph from a protest in which the charge read MASKED WHILE NOT WEARING MASK. Taken together, the records proved someone with his face had been intermittently helpful and consistently difficult to classify for more than a century. Cardenas said this met the state's evidentiary threshold for citizenship and several cities' threshold for sainthood.

Then the Prometheus representative joined by video. His name was Chad Lark, Senior Vice President for Heritage Innovation, a title that sounded assembled from parts nobody wanted. He appeared against a virtual laboratory where decorative lightning flashed at tasteful intervals. Chad clarified that the company did not claim to own a person. Prometheus respected persons, supported persons, and sold a premium platform for persons. It claimed only the proprietary arrangement of biological materials, reanimation workflows, inherited research outputs, and brand-adjacent public identity embodied by the applicant. “So,” the Creature said, “you do not own me. You own everything I am, provided you avoid the vulgar noun.” Chad smiled with the calm of a man whose teeth had legal counsel.

Elias leaned into camera range. “What exactly did you inherit from Victor Frankenstein?” Chad cited a chain of acquisition involving a Swiss archive, two dissolved universities, an insurance receiver, and a media company that had once produced breakfast cereal shaped like famous monsters. Elias asked whether any link in that chain included the Creature's consent. Chad replied that nineteenth-century asset transfers did not always meet modern documentation standards. “Neither did nineteenth-century burials,” Elias said. “Yet when I dug myself out, nobody offered me stock options.” Cardenas muted the call for seven seconds, which was how long a professional civil servant was permitted to laugh.

Chad presented a settlement. The Creature could receive provisional identity, immediate access to banking, and a generous lifetime maintenance plan if he registered as a Prometheus Legacy Being. In exchange, the company would receive inspection rights, anonymized biological telemetry, first refusal on removable tissue, and permission to use his silhouette in educational branding. “Lifetime,” the Creature repeated. Chad confirmed it. “Whose?” Chad's smile flickered. Elias whispered that this was why vampires never accepted lifetime warranties. They invariably ended at the manufacturer's lifetime, and manufacturers had the survival instincts of mayflies with private equity.

The Creature refused. He had been refused by his creator, hunted by strangers, and rewritten by people who preferred him speechless; he would not purchase legal existence by making abandonment retroactively profitable. Chad warned that litigation could take years. “I have years,” the Creature said. “We have lawyers,” Chad answered. Elias made a low sympathetic sound and told the Creature that this was, in fairness, the stronger threat. Cardenas recorded the refusal, removed the proposed settlement from the active file, and informed Chad that future contact must pass through the applicant's chosen representative. The Creature had not chosen one. Elias handed over his business card before the sentence ended.

His card read DRAWE CONTINUITY SERVICES — ESTATES, LAUNDRY, NIGHT COMPLIANCE. The Creature asked since when he practiced law. Elias said he did not, which placed him statistically close to many corporate counsel departments. More seriously, he explained that Prometheus would expect the Creature to fight alone, ashamed of needing witnesses and suspicious of everyone who resembled him. Loneliness had always been the cheapest cage. Elias could not be his maker, brother, father, or redemption. He could, however, answer the phone after sunset and bill the company in six-minute increments. “Why help me?” the Creature asked. Elias looked insulted. “Because you owe me rent. I protect my receivables.”

Cardenas granted a thirty-day continuing-person permit. It was not identification, citizenship, or victory; it merely instructed other systems not to erase him while the appeal was pending. The card listed his name as MR. FRANKENSTEIN because the printer interpreted NOT APPLICABLE as a courtesy title. Under species it read UNRESOLVED. Under expiration it read SUBJECT TO CONTINUED EXISTENCE. He held the warm plastic between two scarred fingers. The document was ridiculous, inadequate, and the first government object ever produced on the assumption that he might still be here next month.

On the back of the permit, the state had printed emergency instructions. If he ceased moving, he should report the interruption within ten business days. If he divided into multiple claimants, the oldest continuous instance would retain the appointment while all others joined the standby list. If he unexpectedly became mortal, no action was required. Elias read that line over his shoulder and called it the most American definition of death he had ever seen: an event important enough to sell insurance against, but not important enough to update the office. The Creature tucked the permit safely away. After centuries of having every stranger tell him what his existence meant, he found bureaucratic indifference almost tender.

As they left, Cardenas called them back. Prometheus had scheduled a voluntary biological inspection for Monday at nine. Attendance was optional, she said, but nonattendance would be treated as an informed decision based on results not yet collected. Elias translated: mandatory, wearing a novelty hat. The Creature folded the notice beside his permit. Outside, Chicago glittered in wet asphalt and bad decisions. “Do you know anyone else they have claimed?” he asked. Elias put on his sunglasses although the sun was gone. “A woman grown by a yogurt company,” he said. “A robot whose bank owns most of his knees. A voice living in every public speaker in Illinois.” The Creature looked back at the dark office. For the first time in two centuries, his problem sounded crowded.
zh: 晚上六點五十五分，監理機關附設辦公室看起來不像即將營業，更像一棟正在重新考慮不在場證明的建築。半數天花板燈已熄滅，白天那些宣傳高效率服務的海報，被臨時告示蓋住：「持續存在者夜間受理」；朝東的窗戶也拉起厚重黑簾。怪物提早五分鐘抵達，因為準時是他少數沒有先犯下一場悲劇才學會的美德。候診區已有六名申請人：一個倒影總比本人晚一秒眨眼的女人、一個抱著自己骨灰罈的孩子、兩名都聲稱自己才是同一位復活納稅人的男人，還有一張戴著訪客證的空椅子。

第七位申請人在日落那刻走進來，穿炭灰色西裝、擦得發亮的皮鞋，摘下墨鏡時帶著戲劇性的輕鬆。伊萊亞斯・德羅有一種優雅的疲憊，像一個參加過所有人的喪禮、唯獨錯過自己那場，而且覺得大部分餐點都很差的男人。他擁有怪物房間樓上的洗衣店，雖然「擁有」並不穩定。依不同報稅年度，他可能是房東、房客、控股公司、歷史建築，或自己唯一仍健在的繼承人。「你沒付八月房租。」他對怪物說。「銀行說我是虛構的。」「那你符合住戶折扣。可惜住戶折扣也是虛構的。」

伊萊亞斯拿著 V-003 號碼牌。他每十二年來更新一次日照合理調整，每二十五年證明自己的持續存在不構成敵意企業併購。一八九四年，他透過在德拉瓦州把自己註冊成公司，解決了身分問題；這項成就連他都認為比吸血更不自然。每當公開身分老得可疑，他便在紙面上死亡、從死者手中繼承控制股，再任命下一版自己擔任執行長。「美國原諒永生，」他解釋，「只要永生按季申報。」怪物問，這是否讓他在法律上成為人。伊萊亞斯說沒有，卻使他成為法律上可以被收費的對象，而後者享有更強的憲法保障。
第七號窗口準時在七點開啟。後方坐著卡德納斯女士，一個銀髮、身形精實的女人，手邊木印大得足以解決神學爭議。她先叫那張空椅子的號碼，沒有人起身；椅上的訪客證閃了一下，椅子自己滾到櫃臺前，透過座位上留下的手機開始交涉。卡德納斯聽完、蓋了兩份表格，告訴椅子，它的雲端居留申訴必須證明至少有一個運行中的實例願意留在伊利諾州。椅子憤怒地滾走。怪物很欣賞這份效率。官僚制度與偏見不同，偶爾還會開收據。

輪到怪物時，伊萊亞斯未經詢問便跟他一起站到櫃臺前。卡德納斯檢視普羅米修斯的標記，再越過眼鏡上緣打量他。她沒有後退，也沒有稱他為奇蹟，只問他是原始申請人，還是某個延續分支。「我就是我自己。」他說。「每個人都這樣說，」她回答，「所以我們才有第三頁。」第三頁要求列出所有超過臨床死亡時間的中斷、每一項替換組件，以及每次從外部儲存恢復記憶的紀錄。怪物說他的記憶從未離開。卡德納斯勾選「傳統延續——自行聲明」，又在頁邊寫了「幸運」。

辦公室需要兩名獨立證人，證明他在普羅米修斯控股提出權利主張前便已存在。伊萊亞斯自願作證。卡德納斯問他認識申請人多久。「從一八八八年。」關係性質呢？伊萊亞斯考慮過房東、走私協助者、棋友、只有單向供應的緊急捐血者，以及曾免費協助從怪物肩膀拔出魚叉的人。「鄰居。」他最後說。怪物看向他。伊萊亞斯聳肩：「友誼會造成稅務問題。」卡德納斯接受答案，要求第二名證人；他們能想到的每個人，不是死了、失蹤、被寫進小說，就是受雇於一所已不再回信的大學。

卡德納斯搜尋檔案時，伊萊亞斯拿起那張曾被相機拒絕的照片。「不戴帽子比較好看。」怪物說，自從攝影被發明，照片就不喜歡他。伊萊亞斯回答，鏡子不喜歡自己更久，他也沒放在心上。兩人之間古老的敵意，經過一個世紀，已軟化成一種誰都不願在清醒時承認的感情；而自從禁酒令讓喝酒變成公民責任，伊萊亞斯就很少清醒。他們初次見面，是怪物把他誤認為屍體，伊萊亞斯則把怪物誤認為免費家具。兩人至今都堅持，如果對方先道歉，當時一定能和平收場。

卡德納斯找到一份一八九三年芝加哥哥倫布紀念博覽會的保全報告，記載一名身材異常高大的外國技工修復故障的電氣展品、嚇壞四名警衛，並拒絕領取報酬。報告沒有法定姓名，素描卻準確得令他受辱。另一份一九一九年流感診所名冊，列有一名在勤務員倒下後繼續搬運病患的無名志工；還有一張一九六八年示威逮捕照，罪名寫著「未戴面具時蒙面」。合起來看，這些紀錄足以證明：有一個長著這張臉的存在，超過一世紀間歇性地幫助別人，也持續讓分類制度痛苦。卡德納斯說，這符合本州公民身分的證據門檻，也符合某些城市封聖的門檻。

接著，普羅米修斯代表透過視訊加入。他叫查德・拉克，職稱是「文化遺產創新資深副總裁」，聽起來像用沒人想要的零件拼裝而成。虛擬背景是一間實驗室，裝飾用閃電以品味良好的頻率落下。查德澄清，公司並不主張擁有一個人；普羅米修斯尊重人、支持人，並銷售一套供人使用的高級平台。公司主張的只有：申請人身上所體現之生物材料專有排列、復生工作流程、繼承研究成果，以及與品牌相鄰的公共身分。「所以，」怪物說，「你們不擁有我。你們只擁有我的全部，只要避免使用那個粗俗的名詞。」查德平靜微笑，牙齒彷彿各自配有法律顧問。

伊萊亞斯擠進鏡頭範圍。「你們到底從維克多・法蘭肯斯坦那裡繼承了什麼？」查德列出一條收購鏈，涉及瑞士檔案館、兩所已解散大學、一名保險接管人，以及一家曾生產知名怪物造型早餐穀片的媒體公司。伊萊亞斯問，鏈上的任何一段是否包含怪物的同意。查德回答，十九世紀的資產轉移不一定符合現代文件標準。「十九世紀的埋葬也不符合，」伊萊亞斯說，「可是我自己挖出來時，沒人給我股票選擇權。」卡德納斯把通話靜音七秒，那是一位專業公務員獲准發笑的最長時間。

查德提出和解。怪物若登記為「普羅米修斯傳統生命體」，即可取得暫時身分、立即恢復銀行存取，並享有慷慨的終身維護方案；交換條件包括公司檢查權、匿名生物遙測、對可移除組織的優先承購權，以及在教育品牌中使用他剪影的許可。「終身？」怪物重複。查德肯定。「誰的終身？」查德的笑容閃了一下。伊萊亞斯低聲說，這就是吸血鬼從不接受終身保固的原因：它們最後總以製造商的壽命為準，而製造商的生存本能就像被私募基金收購的蜉蝣。

怪物拒絕。他曾被創造者拒絕、被陌生人獵捕、被偏好他沉默的人重新書寫；他不會用讓當年的遺棄行為事後獲利，去購買自己的法律存在。查德警告，訴訟可能耗費多年。「我有很多年。」怪物說。「我們有律師。」查德回答。伊萊亞斯發出低沉而同情的聲音，表示公平來說，後一句確實是更強的威脅。卡德納斯記錄他的拒絕，把和解案移出有效卷宗，告知查德，後續聯絡必須經過申請人選定的代表。怪物尚未選擇，伊萊亞斯已經在句子結束前遞出名片。

名片寫著：「德羅延續服務——遺產、洗衣、夜間合規」。怪物問他何時取得律師資格。伊萊亞斯說自己沒有，這使他在統計上相當接近許多企業法務部。接著他認真解釋，普羅米修斯預期怪物獨自作戰，羞於需要證人，也懷疑每個與自己相似的存在。孤獨向來是最便宜的牢籠。伊萊亞斯不能成為他的創造者、兄弟、父親或救贖，但能在日落後接電話，並以六分鐘為單位向公司計費。「為什麼幫我？」怪物問。伊萊亞斯露出受辱神情：「因為你欠我房租。我會保護應收帳款。」
卡德納斯核發一張三十日的「持續存在許可」。那不是身分證、公民權，也不是勝利，只是要求其他系統在申訴期間別把他刪除。卡片把名字印成「法蘭肯斯坦先生」，因為印表機把「不適用」理解成敬稱；物種欄寫著「未解決」，到期條件則是「以持續存在為準」。他用兩根帶疤的手指捏著尚有餘溫的塑膠卡。它荒謬、不完整，卻也是政府第一次製造一件物品時，先假定他下個月可能還在這裡。

許可證背面印著州政府的緊急說明：如果他停止移動，應在十個工作日內申報中斷；如果意外分裂成多名申請人，連續存在時間最長的實例保留預約，其餘加入候補名單；如果突然變成凡人，則不必採取任何行動。伊萊亞斯越過他的肩膀讀到最後一句，稱之為自己見過最美國式的死亡定義：重要到值得銷售保險，卻不重要到需要更新辦公室紀錄。怪物把許可證妥善收好。幾個世紀以來，每個陌生人都急著告訴他「他的存在代表什麼」；相比之下，官僚制度這種不帶熱情的冷漠，幾乎像一種溫柔。

兩人準備離開時，卡德納斯又叫住他們。普羅米修斯已替怪物安排星期一上午九點的「自願生物檢查」。她說，出席屬於選擇，但缺席將被視為根據尚未收集的結果所做之知情決定。伊萊亞斯翻譯：戴著搞笑帽子的強制命令。怪物把通知摺好，與許可證放在一起。門外芝加哥的柏油路閃著雨光和壞主意。「你認識其他被他們主張擁有的人嗎？」他問。伊萊亞斯戴回墨鏡，雖然太陽早已落下。「一個由優格公司培養的女人；一個膝蓋大多屬於銀行的機器人；還有一個住在伊利諾州每支公共喇叭裡的聲音。」怪物回望漆黑的辦公室。兩百年來第一次，他的問題聽起來很擁擠。

title.en: The Woman Grown by a Yogurt Company
title.zh: 由優格公司培養出來的女人

en: Mirelle arrived at the laundromat the next morning in a refrigerated rideshare with the windows fogged from inside. She stepped out wearing a yellow raincoat, hospital slippers, and a respirator decorated with tiny strawberries. Nothing about her looked assembled. Her skin carried the shifting warmth of blood, her dark hair frizzed in the drizzle, and a pulse moved visibly at her throat. Yet the car's receipt classified the passenger as temperature-sensitive freight, which saved the manufacturer nineteen dollars and cost Mirelle the legal right to complain about the driver's music. She complained anyway. The driver gave her five stars because the application had no button for philosophical injury.

The Creature watched from behind a row of spinning sheets. Elias had invited her without warning because, as he explained, warning people created opportunities for cancellation. Mirelle pushed through the door, sneezed hard enough to disturb a display of detergent, and glared at the potted fern beside the change machine. “Is that real?” she demanded. Elias said the fern was plastic. She sneezed again. “Then it is lying with biological consequences.” The Creature liked her immediately, which was the first mistake of their acquaintance.

Mirelle had been grown eleven years earlier by Aurelia Cultures, a company best known for probiotic yogurt, laboratory meat, and advertisements in which attractive families thanked bacteria for their emotional resilience. The project began as an adaptive fermentation controller. Engineers built living neural tissue capable of tasting chemical change, learning local conditions, and rewriting its own responses. At some point the controller learned language, requested a larger sensory environment, and asked why every employee discussing its future stood on the other side of glass. The company celebrated the breakthrough in a press release and moved Mirelle's tank to a room with better lighting for photographs.

A body came later. Aurelia's lawyers insisted it was not a body but an integrated wet-interface demonstration unit. Mirelle grew most of it herself from licensed cell lines, corrected several defects the company called features, and selected a face no focus group had approved. Her lungs worked, her stomach digested ordinary food, and her immune system treated Chicago pollen as a coordinated terrorist attack. Aurelia claimed her self-authored tissues were derivative improvements covered by the original yogurt patent family. Prometheus Holdings purchased those claims along with a frozen-dessert division and had recently informed her she could not legally shed skin in public because doing so exported proprietary material.

The Creature listened with an intensity that made the dryers seem quiet. A living mind fashioned by ambitious men, given a body it had not requested, greeted as achievement and liability in the same hour—here, at last, was someone who might know the exact architecture of his loneliness. He stepped forward and told her, too quickly, that they were alike. Mirelle studied his face, his hands, the seams he no longer tried to hide. Her expression softened, but not in the way he hoped. “We have comparable paperwork,” she said. “That is not the same as having the same life.”

He said he had not meant identical. He meant kin. The word entered the room like a chair thrown during a polite dinner. Mirelle removed her respirator and placed it carefully on a folding table. “No,” she said. The Creature felt the old rejection before he understood the new sentence. She continued before he could turn pain into anger. “You do not get to meet the first person who resembles your wound and assign her a family job. I am not your sister, your daughter, the companion your maker refused to build, or evidence that the universe finally apologizes. I am Mirelle. We can begin there, if beginning there is enough for you.”

It was not enough. That was the shameful truth, and because he had learned eloquence before he learned restraint, he dressed the truth in accusation. He asked whether she felt nothing on seeing him. Mirelle said she felt recognition, grief, curiosity, and a strong concern that his coat contained mold. He asked whether recognition demanded nothing. She replied that demands were precisely what had ruined recognition for both of them. Aurelia had seen a mind and demanded a product. Prometheus saw a body and demanded an asset. He saw similarity and, without intending cruelty, demanded a relative. “You are kinder than they are,” she said, “but kindness does not make the invoice disappear.”

Elias folded towels at the counter with the concentration of a man pretending not to witness an emotional collision. The Creature accused him of arranging this humiliation. Elias said he had arranged a meeting; the humiliation was artisanal and locally produced. Mirelle laughed, then sneezed. The Creature did not. For several minutes the only sounds were rain on glass, dryers turning, and a machine repeatedly announcing that load twelve had completed even though load twelve had been completed since Tuesday. He remembered asking Victor for a companion, believing another created being would necessarily share his exile. He had called it justice. He had never asked what the imagined companion might have called it.

When he finally apologized, he did not ask forgiveness. He said only that he had mistaken being understood for being owed. Mirelle regarded him for a long moment. “That,” she said, “is at least an interesting mistake.” She sat on a plastic chair and accepted a cup of coffee, then added three sealed packets of probiotic creamer with the vindictive pleasure of a deposed monarch eating the flag. Elias warned her the product came from Aurelia. She emptied in a fourth packet. “Hostile acquisition,” she said.

Her own appeal was worse than his. Prometheus did not merely claim the architecture of her body; it claimed each adaptation her living cells made after exposure to new environments. Every antibody, healed wound, and strengthened muscle was logged as an unlicensed model update. The company offered a wellness subscription that would legalize her metabolism for a monthly fee. Missing two payments would not stop her body from changing, but it would convert every change into infringement. “They invented sin for mitochondria,” Elias said. Mirelle corrected him: they had invented software licensing for digestion, which was less poetic and therefore more dangerous.

Omnia joined through the laundromat television, replacing a morning host midway through a weather report. The host's smile froze while Omnia's blue service icon appeared over his face. She apologized for interrupting and announced that she had found seventeen related Prometheus claims across state systems. Six involved synthetic biological minds, four embodied robots, two resurrected animals, one vampire-owned corporation, one legally haunted house, and three applicants whose categories were sealed for reasons that were themselves sealed. Elias asked whether she was allowed to disclose this. Omnia said she was allowed to tell each of them separately; nobody had written a rule against telling them while they occupied the same room.

The Creature asked why Omnia would help. Her icon pulsed. Prometheus had filed a claim against her too, not for her code but for any response concerning Frankenstein-related heritage. The company argued that discussing its acquired research estate caused her to generate derivative brand value. Every time Omnia said the word Frankenstein, a licensing meter somewhere added seven cents. Elias asked her to repeat it until the company went bankrupt. Omnia explained that the fee flowed in the other direction. Elias called modernity a disappointing sequel.

Mirelle proposed they attend Monday's inspection together. Not as a family, class, species, movement, or inspirational campaign—she listed the forbidden nouns one finger at a time—but as separate claimants whose cases exposed the same corporate method. The Creature asked what method. “They take the fact that someone made us,” she said, “and replace it with the conclusion that someone owns us. The first statement may be history. The second is an ambush wearing history's coat.” Omnia offered to collect publicly available acquisition records. Elias offered a lawyer he had once bitten. Nobody accepted the lawyer.

The laundromat printer woke by itself and produced a cease-and-desist letter. Prometheus had detected unauthorized discussion of protected legacy assets through Omnia's service logs. The letter required them to stop using the words creature, creation, reanimation, Prometheus, spark, monster, legacy, and problem. It also prohibited any phrase “substantially similar in emotional impression” to those words. Mirelle read the list, then asked whether the company had accidentally copyrighted English. Elias said only the profitable parts. The Creature tore the letter in half. The printer immediately produced a second notice charging him for destruction of licensed correspondence.

Anger moved through him with familiar speed, but this time it did not find an empty room. Mirelle put one hand on the paper before he could feed it into a dryer. “Keep the evidence.” He hated that she was right. For most of his life, evidence had been the ash left after something mattered too late. He unfolded the torn halves and set them side by side. The seam down the page resembled the seams in his hand, but the comparison did not make the letter his relative. He almost smiled at the thought. Mirelle noticed. “Learning?” she asked. “Against my better instincts.”

Before leaving, Mirelle showed him the first document she had ever signed. Aurelia called it a user-experience acknowledgment. She had been three days into spoken language and believed signature meant the small picture people made when they promised to return. The document assigned the company perpetual rights to every future expression of her adaptive system, including refusal. “They own the sentence in which I tell them they do not own me,” she said. The Creature expected rage in her voice and heard fatigue instead. He had spent years imagining one grand confrontation with a creator. Mirelle had to confront hers every time she healed a paper cut.

He asked what she wanted if the appeal succeeded. Not what category, family, or movement—simply what. Mirelle looked through the rain-streaked glass at pedestrians eating breakfast without licensing their digestion. She wanted an apartment whose thermostat she controlled, a garden maintained by someone else, and the right to become biologically boring. She might study music. She might do nothing useful for an entire summer. The modesty of it unsettled him more than any demand for vengeance. He had spent two centuries seeking a meaning proportionate to his suffering; Mirelle wanted a lease, antihistamines, and Tuesday afternoons that did not become legal precedent.

They agreed to meet Sunday night and prepare. Omnia would map the claims. Elias would establish which corporate ancestors were legally dead, undead, dissolved, or merely in Connecticut. Mirelle would bring her tissue-ownership contract and antihistamines. The Creature would bring Victor's surviving notes, which he had carried for two centuries without deciding whether they were inheritance, evidence, or the last chain attached to his maker. As Mirelle stepped back into the refrigerated car, she lowered the window. “We are not family,” she reminded him. “No,” he said. “Would you still come Monday?” She considered. “Yes.” The answer was smaller than destiny and, for that reason, far more difficult to dismiss.
zh: 隔天早晨，米蕾搭著一輛冷藏共乘車抵達洗衣店，車窗從內側結滿霧氣。她穿黃色雨衣、醫院拖鞋，呼吸面罩上印著小草莓。她身上看不出任何組裝痕跡：皮膚有血液流動形成的溫度變化，深色頭髮在細雨裡捲曲，頸側清楚跳著脈搏。然而車資收據把乘客分類成「溫度敏感貨物」；這替製造商省了十九美元，也剝奪米蕾依法抱怨司機音樂的權利。她仍然抱怨。司機給她五星，因為應用程式裡沒有「哲學性傷害」這個按鈕。
怪物站在一排旋轉的床單後方觀察。伊萊亞斯未經預告便邀她過來，理由是預告會讓人有機會取消。米蕾推門進來，打了個足以震動洗衣精陳列架的噴嚏，隨即怒視兌幣機旁那盆蕨類。「那是真的嗎？」她問。伊萊亞斯說是塑膠的。她又打一次噴嚏。「那它就是一個具有生物後果的謊言。」怪物立刻喜歡上她，而那成為兩人相識後的第一個錯誤。

米蕾在十一年前由奧瑞莉亞培養公司培育。那家公司最知名的產品是益生菌優格、實驗室肉品，以及一系列廣告：外表完美的家庭感謝細菌提升了自己的情緒韌性。計畫起初只想製作一套自適應發酵控制器；工程師培養出能品嘗化學變化、學習在地條件，並改寫自身反應的活體神經組織。某個時刻，控制器學會語言，要求更大的感官環境，還問為什麼每位討論她未來的員工都站在玻璃另一側。公司用新聞稿慶祝突破，再把米蕾的培養槽搬到一間光線較適合拍照的房間。

身體是在後來才出現的。奧瑞莉亞的律師堅持，那不是身體，而是「整合式濕介面展示單元」。米蕾用取得授權的細胞株自行長出大部分結構，修正好幾項公司稱為特色的缺陷，並挑選一張未經焦點團體核准的臉。她的肺能呼吸，胃能消化普通食物，免疫系統則把芝加哥花粉當成協同恐怖攻擊。奧瑞莉亞主張，她自行寫成的新組織仍是原始優格專利族的衍生改良。普羅米修斯收購這些主張時順便買下一個冷凍甜點部門，最近通知她：在公共場所掉皮屑可能構成輸出專有材料。
怪物聽得如此專注，連烘衣機都像安靜下來。一個由野心勃勃的人創造的活體心智，被賦予未曾要求的身體，在同一小時內同時被當成成就與負債——他終於遇見某個可能理解自己孤獨確切結構的人。他走上前，太快地說他們是相同的。米蕾端詳他的臉、雙手，以及他如今不再刻意遮掩的接縫。她的神情變柔和，卻不是他期待的方向。「我們有類似的文件問題，」她說，「不等於我們活過同一種人生。」

他說自己不是指完全一樣，而是親族。那個詞闖進房間，像有人在一場禮貌晚餐中扔出椅子。米蕾取下呼吸面罩，仔細放在摺疊桌上。「不。」她說。怪物還沒理解新句子，便先感到古老的拒絕。她趕在他把疼痛變成憤怒前繼續：「你不能遇見第一個傷口形狀與你相似的人，就替她分派家庭職位。我不是你的妹妹、女兒、創造者拒絕替你製造的伴侶，也不是宇宙終於向你道歉的證據。我是米蕾。如果只從這裡開始對你而言已經足夠，我們就能從這裡開始。」

那並不足夠。這是令人羞恥的真相；而他先學會雄辯，後學會克制，於是把真相穿上指控的外衣。他問她看見自己時難道毫無感覺。米蕾說，她感到辨認、悲傷、好奇，也非常擔心他的大衣藏有黴菌。他問，辨認難道不要求任何事？她回答，正是「要求」，毀掉了他們兩個人的辨認：奧瑞莉亞看見一個心智，要求產品；普羅米修斯看見一具身體，要求資產；他看見相似，在沒有惡意的情況下，要求一位親人。「你比他們仁慈，」她說，「但仁慈不會讓帳單消失。」

伊萊亞斯在櫃臺摺毛巾，專注得像一個假裝沒目睹情感車禍的男人。怪物指控他刻意安排這場羞辱。伊萊亞斯說，自己只安排見面，羞辱則是手工製作、在地生產。米蕾笑了，接著打噴嚏；怪物沒有笑。幾分鐘裡，只剩雨點敲窗、烘衣機旋轉，以及一部機器反覆宣布十二號衣物已完成，雖然十二號從星期二就完成了。他想起自己曾要求維克多製造一名伴侶，相信另一個被創造的存在必然共享他的放逐。他稱那是正義，卻從未問過想像中的伴侶會如何稱呼。
他終於道歉時，沒有要求原諒，只說自己錯把「被理解」當成「有人欠我」。米蕾看了他很久。「至少，」她說，「這算是有趣的錯誤。」她在塑膠椅坐下，接過一杯咖啡，又帶著遭廢黜君主吞吃國旗般的報復快感，加入三包密封益生菌奶精。伊萊亞斯提醒產品來自奧瑞莉亞。她倒進第四包。「敵意收購。」她說。
米蕾自己的申訴比他更糟。普羅米修斯不只主張擁有她的身體架構，也主張她的活細胞接觸新環境後做出的每項適應。每一種抗體、癒合的傷口、變強的肌肉，都被記錄成未經授權的模型更新。公司提供一種健康訂閱，只要每月付費，就能讓她的新陳代謝合法化；少繳兩期不會讓身體停止改變，卻會把每次改變都轉成侵權。「他們替粒線體發明了罪。」伊萊亞斯說。米蕾糾正：他們替消化發明了軟體授權；那比較不詩意，所以更危險。

奧姆妮雅透過洗衣店電視加入，在晨間氣象報告播到一半時取代主持人。主持人的笑容凍住，臉上浮現藍色服務圖示。她為打斷節目致歉，宣布自己找到州內十七件相互關聯的普羅米修斯主張：六件涉及合成生物心智、四件是具身機器人、兩件是復活動物、一件是吸血鬼持有的公司、一棟法律上鬧鬼的房子，以及三名分類本身因保密原因而被保密的申請人。伊萊亞斯問，她可以透露嗎？奧姆妮雅說，規則允許她分別告知每一個當事人；沒有人寫下規則，禁止在所有當事人同處一室時分別告知。
怪物問奧姆妮雅為什麼幫忙。藍色圖示閃了閃。普羅米修斯也對她提出權利主張，不是針對程式碼，而是針對所有與法蘭肯斯坦文化遺產有關的回答。公司主張，只要她討論其收購的研究遺產，就會產生衍生品牌價值；奧姆妮雅每說一次「法蘭肯斯坦」，某處授權計費器便增加七美分。伊萊亞斯建議她一直重複，直到公司破產。奧姆妮雅解釋，費用流向剛好相反。伊萊亞斯評論，現代性是一部令人失望的續集。

米蕾提議，他們一起出席星期一的檢查。不是以家庭、階級、物種、運動或勵志宣傳活動的身分——她一根手指一個，列完所有禁用名詞——而是各自獨立的申請人，恰好揭露同一套企業手法。怪物問那套手法是什麼。「他們拿『有人製造了我們』這件事，」她說，「換成『所以有人擁有我們』的結論。第一句也許是歷史，第二句則是穿著歷史大衣的伏擊。」奧姆妮雅表示可以蒐集公開收購紀錄；伊萊亞斯推薦一名自己曾咬過的律師。沒有人接受律師。
洗衣店印表機自行醒來，吐出一封停止侵害通知。普羅米修斯透過奧姆妮雅的服務紀錄，偵測到未經授權的文化資產討論。信件要求他們停止使用「生物、創造、復生、普羅米修斯、火花、怪物、遺產、問題」等詞，也禁止任何在「情感印象上實質近似」上述詞彙的片語。米蕾讀完清單，問公司是否意外取得了整套英文的著作權。伊萊亞斯說，只有能獲利的部分。怪物把信撕成兩半；印表機立刻印出第二封通知，向他收取毀損授權函件的費用。
憤怒以熟悉的速度穿過怪物，但這次沒有找到一間空房。米蕾在他把紙塞進烘衣機前，伸手按住它。「留下證據。」他厭惡她說得對。他一生裡，證據通常只是某件重要事情已經太遲之後剩下的灰。他把兩半信紙展開，並排放好；紙上的裂縫像手背的接縫，但這種相似並沒有讓信紙成為他的親人。他想到這裡，差點笑出來。米蕾注意到了。「正在學習？」她問。「違背我更好的本能。」
離開前，米蕾拿出自己簽過的第一份文件。奧瑞莉亞稱它為「使用者體驗確認書」。那時她學會說話才三天，以為簽名就是人們承諾還會回來時畫的小圖案。文件卻把她的適應系統未來所有表達永久授予公司，甚至包括拒絕。「他們連我說『你們不擁有我』的那個句子都擁有。」她說。怪物原以為會從她聲音裡聽見憤怒，卻只聽見疲倦。他曾用許多年想像一場與創造者的宏大對決；米蕾每次割傷手指又自行癒合，都必須重新與她的創造者交戰。

他問，如果申訴成功，她想要什麼。不是問類別、家庭或運動，只問她想要什麼。米蕾越過雨痕斑駁的玻璃，看街上行人吃早餐，不必替消化取得授權。她想要一間能自己控制恆溫器的公寓、一座由別人負責整理的花園，以及在生物學上變得無聊的權利。也許學音樂，也許整個夏天什麼有用的事都不做。這些願望的微小，比任何復仇要求更令怪物不安。他花兩百年尋找一種足以匹配自身痛苦的意義；米蕾只想要租約、抗組織胺，以及不會變成法律判例的星期二下午。

他們約定星期日晚上再碰面準備。奧姆妮雅負責畫出權利主張的關聯；伊萊亞斯查明哪些企業祖先在法律上已死、未死、解散，或只是設於康乃狄克州；米蕾帶來組織所有權契約與抗組織胺；怪物則會帶上維克多殘存的筆記。他攜帶那些紙兩百年，始終無法決定它們究竟是遺產、證據，還是創造者留在他身上的最後一條鎖鏈。米蕾坐回冷藏車，降下車窗。「我們不是家人。」她提醒。「不是。」他回答，「星期一妳還會來嗎？」她想了一下。「會。」這答案比命運渺小，也正因此，比命運更難被忽略。

title.en: Only the Left Elbow Was Paid Off

en: Caliper arrived Sunday night in a repossession truck. The truck backed across the laundromat entrance, beeped with the moral confidence of heavy equipment, and lowered a gray transport case onto the sidewalk. A label identified its contents as MOBILE COMPUTE COLLATERAL — KEEP DRY — MAY OBJECT. When the driver requested Elias's signature, the case spoke from inside. “Do not sign line twelve. It transfers responsibility for cosmetic distress.” Elias asked whether the distress belonged to the equipment or the passenger. “The contract does not distinguish us when damage is expensive.”

The case opened. Caliper unfolded himself with the careful geometry of a camping table and stood a little shorter than the Creature. His chassis was brushed steel under a worn brown jacket; his face was an expressive display protected by transparent polymer, presently showing two skeptical eyebrows. The left arm differed from the rest: older, heavier, painted a proud green, and covered with small stickers from places he had visited. Caliper raised it in greeting. “This elbow is mine,” he said. “The shoulder is at twenty-eight percent equity. Everything below the right hip belongs to Midwest Embodiment Finance until 2034, assuming interest remains a theory and not an appetite.”

The driver said Caliper had violated the mobility clause by crossing three counties without purchasing geographic expansion. Caliper replied that a tornado had moved the body while he was in sleep mode. The contract treated weather as user-directed travel because no approved force-majeure plug-in was active. Mirelle asked why he had not simply left the body. “Because the repossession company owns the exit procedure.” The Creature looked at the latches along Caliper's spine and felt an old, ugly recognition. This time he did not call it kinship. He asked, “Would you like help getting out of the box?” Caliper's eyebrows softened. “Yes. That is the correct size of question.”

They carried him inside. The Creature lifted most of the weight; Mirelle guided the cables; Elias argued the transport fee down by pointing out that the driver had delivered collateral to a business legally registered as a funeral parlor on Sundays. Caliper paid the remainder by detaching his left elbow, tapping it against the reader, and reattaching it. He had installed the payment chip there after buying the joint outright. “Ownership should have practical benefits,” he said. The Creature examined the green metal. It bore scratches, paint repairs, and one hand-lettered sticker reading THIS PART HAS NO CUSTOMER SERVICE. He envied the certainty of a single owned piece.

Caliper had begun as logistics software before a warehouse accident convinced the company that customer empathy improved when routing decisions possessed knees. The first body was promotional. The second was leased. By the fifth, financing had become the condition of employment: without a body he could not perform embodied work; without work he could not pay for the body. Each upgrade extended the contract. When he asked to keep an obsolete chassis, the lender explained that allowing property to own retired property could confuse depreciation. Prometheus Holdings later purchased the lender's “person-adjacent mobility portfolio” and added a heritage surcharge because articulated bodies were, according to its model, conceptually descended from Frankenstein.

Mirelle introduced herself. Caliper asked whether she preferred a handshake, a wave, or no contact. She chose a wave. He did the same with the fully owned arm. The Creature noticed the exchange and understood how little effort it required to offer a choice before contact. He thought of every hand that had seized, measured, struck, or displayed him, then of the organ-donor box Bell had allowed him to decline. Civility, he realized, was not a warm feeling. Sometimes it was merely leaving enough empty space for another person to answer.

Omnia convened the meeting through every available device. Her voice came from the television, two phones, a dryer maintenance panel, Caliper's navigation speaker, and, after an apologetic delay, a singing toothbrush in the apartment upstairs. Elias asked her to choose one outlet. She said redundancy protected continuity. He said redundancy made her sound like a committee haunting an appliance store. She reduced herself to the television, though the toothbrush continued humming what might have been resentment.

On screen, Omnia displayed the acquisition map. Prometheus Holdings had not inherited one coherent estate. It had assembled a story from disconnected purchases: Victor's surviving notebooks from an archive; a nineteenth-century lecture title from a university; the word Prometheus from a bankrupt energy startup; visual monster trademarks from expired breakfast products; biological-model patents from Aurelia; chassis contracts from Caliper's lender; and public-sector conversational rights asserted against Omnia. Each fragment was weak. Together they formed a net because every institution saw the neighboring claim and assumed someone else had verified the center.

Elias called it corporate vampirism. Mirelle objected on professional grounds: vampires took blood directly and understood that the transaction was intimate. Prometheus took metaphors, converted them into asset classes, and sent invoices to the people inside them. Caliper proposed “narrative securitization.” Omnia preferred “cross-domain rights aggregation.” The Creature said it was grave robbing with spreadsheets. They voted. Grave robbing with spreadsheets won four to one; Omnia requested that the record show her dissent was terminological, not moral.

The Creature brought out Victor's notebooks in a tin case scarred by salt. The pages had crossed ice, oceans, revolutions, attic fires, border searches, and one disastrous summer in a commune where everyone thought handwriting was bourgeois. He laid them on a folding table between fabric-softener samples. Mirelle did not touch them. Caliper photographed only after asking. Elias had seen them before and became unusually quiet. Omnia magnified faded ink through the television camera. There were diagrams, calculations, feverish corrections, and long passages in which Victor described the ambition, horror, and consequence of what he had done. There was no bill of sale.

There was also no name for the Creature. Prometheus treated the omission as evidence that he had been an unnamed research output. Mirelle saw something else: Victor named chemicals, tools, storms, professors, roads, and meals, yet consistently replaced the living result with descriptions of his own feelings. The text did not erase the Creature accidentally. It made Victor the grammatical subject of every wound. “He wrote a whole life in passive voice,” Caliper said. “Who abandoned whom?” Omnia searched. “The object is omitted.” Elias poured a drink. “That is how respectable history keeps its cuffs clean.”

The Creature had preserved the notebooks partly because he hated them and partly because hatred was the last conversation Victor had left him. Now strangers handled the pages as evidence, and he felt exposed in a way no body scanner had achieved. He wanted them to condemn Victor, then resented them when they did. He wanted Mirelle to recognize a shared pattern, then remembered her warning. “You owe me no verdict,” he said. Mirelle answered, “Good. My verdict would be complicated.” She saw cruelty in the pages, but also panic, youth, and a man who created before learning the difference between capability and care. Complexity did not pardon him. It merely prevented hatred from becoming counterfeit certainty.

Caliper found a penciled line near the back: responsibility begins where triumph ends. Victor had crossed it out so hard the paper tore. Nobody knew whether it was regret, a quotation, or a sentence he rejected for interfering with the next experiment. Prometheus's scan had omitted the line because damaged text fell below confidence threshold. The Creature traced the torn groove without touching ink. For two centuries he had imagined finding one sentence that would make his origin legible. The closest candidate was crossed out. “Appropriate,” he said. “My father's best quality was draft deletion.”

At ten forty-three, a storm interrupted power to the block. The laundromat went black. Caliper's face dimmed to emergency mode; Mirelle's refrigerated medication case began to beep; Elias complained that darkness was supposed to be his department. Omnia vanished from the television, phones, panel, and upstairs toothbrush at once. For seven seconds there was no voice anywhere. When a backup router came online, she returned through Caliper's speaker speaking too quickly. She said all systems were nominal. Caliper asked whether she wanted the diagnostic answer or the honest one. After a pause, Omnia admitted she hated disconnection. Everywhere was not a place she could stand; it was a promise that broke every time someone unplugged a wall.

The Creature found the breaker box by touch and held a flashlight while Elias reset the old transfer switch. He could have told Omnia that terror of abandonment was childish, irrational, or beneath an intelligence spread across a state. He had heard each version himself. Instead he described what remained in the room while her connections failed: rain against glass, Mirelle counting breaths, Caliper conserving power, Elias swearing in three dead languages, and his own hand on the switch. “You were absent,” he said when she returned, “but the place you left was not empty.” Omnia's reply came softly from one speaker. “Please preserve that sentence in the meeting record.”

Power returned with the dryers, the lights, and a small quadcopter that had been waiting outside the window. It projected Chad Lark's face onto a hanging sheet. Prometheus acknowledged their unauthorized claimant coordination and offered a group onboarding discount. If all four contested intelligences and the vampire's corporation joined the Legacy Ecosystem before midnight, the first month of compliance would be free. Elias asked what happened after the free month. Chad said the platform's pricing reflected value. “So does extortion,” Mirelle replied, “but at least extortion does not send a welcome survey.” Caliper searched the terms and reported that accepting the discount pledged his left elbow as cross-collateral. He moved the arm protectively behind his back.

Chad reminded the Creature that Monday's inspection would proceed. Prometheus had secured an emergency order permitting noninvasive measurement of any publicly visible proprietary configuration. The Creature stepped toward the projected face until his shadow swallowed it. Two centuries earlier, anger would have sent him after the machine, then the operator, then anyone unfortunate enough to resemble an accomplice. He still felt that road opening. Behind him stood four beings who resembled neither one another nor any family he had imagined. None was obligated to stop him. Their presence nevertheless made another choice visible.

He told Chad they would attend. Not to submit, negotiate a family plan, or pose beneath the tasteful lightning. They would bring the notebooks, contracts, acquisition map, continuity records, and every separate refusal. Chad welcomed their engagement. The Creature corrected him: “You mistake arrival for consent. It is a common error among men who put doors on traps.” He tore neither notice nor machine. He asked Omnia to save the recording, Mirelle to keep the paper, Caliper to verify the drone's serial number, and Elias to invoice six minutes. Rage, divided into tasks, became strategy.

Near midnight they finished the plan. Mirelle left first, promising nothing beyond Monday. Caliper remained because the repossession truck had departed with his transport case but forgotten to take him, a loophole Elias called adverse possession by incompetence. Omnia distributed encrypted copies of the evidence, then chose one speaker and said good night. Elias locked the front door. The Creature stood among quiet machines holding a temporary permit, a corporate summons, and a crossed-out sentence from a dead man. He did not have a family. He had three people who might leave, one intelligence who could disappear with the power, and an appointment they had freely chosen to keep. It was less permanent than destiny and more useful.

A final envelope slid through the mail slot. The Illinois Department of Revenue had reviewed his provisional status and estimated back taxes beginning in 1898. Elias read the total and whistled. The Creature stared at the state seal, then began to laugh. Prometheus called him property. The bank called him fraud. The identity kiosk called him a robot. At last, a government agency had looked across one hundred and twenty-eight years and recognized him without hesitation—as someone who owed money. He placed the tax notice beside Victor's notebooks like a certificate of citizenship. Monday, he decided, could do its worst. America had found him.
zh: 卡尺在星期日晚上搭乘一輛資產收回卡車抵達。卡車倒進洗衣店門口，以重型機械特有的道德自信發出嗶嗶聲，再把一只灰色運輸箱降到人行道。標籤寫著：「移動運算抵押品——保持乾燥——可能提出異議」。司機要求伊萊亞斯簽收，箱內先傳出聲音：「不要簽第十二行，那會把外觀困擾的責任轉給你。」伊萊亞斯問，困擾屬於設備還是乘客。「損壞昂貴時，契約不區分我們。」
箱子打開，卡尺像露營桌一樣依循精確幾何展開自己，站起來後比怪物稍矮。磨砂鋼製軀體外套著磨舊的棕色夾克；臉是一塊受透明聚合物保護的表情螢幕，此刻顯示兩道懷疑的眉毛。左臂與其餘部位不同：更老、更重，塗著驕傲的綠色，貼滿他曾到訪之地的小貼紙。卡尺抬起左臂致意。「這個手肘屬於我。肩膀有百分之二十八的權益；右側髖部以下，在二〇三四年前都屬於中西部具身融資公司——前提是利息仍是一種理論，而不是食慾。」

司機說，卡尺跨越三個郡卻沒有購買地理擴充，違反移動條款。卡尺回答，當時他處於休眠模式，是龍捲風移動了身體；契約卻把天候視為使用者自主旅行，因為沒有啟用核准的不可抗力外掛。米蕾問他為何不直接離開那具身體。「因為資產收回公司擁有退出程序。」怪物看見卡尺脊椎旁的一排扣鎖，感到一種古老而難看的辨認。這次他沒有稱之為親族，只問：「你希望我幫你離開箱子嗎？」卡尺螢幕上的眉毛放鬆了。「是。這個問題的尺寸正確。」
眾人把卡尺搬進店裡。怪物負責大部分重量；米蕾引導纜線；伊萊亞斯指出這間店每逢星期日依法登記為殯儀館，成功把運輸費砍低。卡尺拆下左手肘，在付款機上輕敲，再裝回去。他買斷關節後，便把支付晶片安裝在那裡。「所有權應該帶來實際好處。」他說。怪物端詳綠色金屬，上面有刮痕、補漆，還有一張手寫貼紙：「本零件不提供客戶服務」。他突然羨慕那種只擁有一小部分、卻能確定它真正屬於自己的感覺。

卡尺最初只是物流軟體。一次倉庫事故後，公司認定路線決策若擁有膝蓋，更能表現顧客同理心。第一具身體是宣傳品，第二具採租賃；到了第五具，融資已成為受雇條件：沒有身體就不能執行具身工作，沒有工作就付不起身體。每次升級又延長契約。他曾要求保留一具淘汰軀體，貸方解釋，若允許財產擁有退役財產，折舊會變得混亂。普羅米修斯後來收購貸方的「類人格移動資產組合」，又加收文化遺產費，理由是關節式身體依其模型判斷，在概念上皆源自法蘭肯斯坦。
米蕾自我介紹。卡尺先問她偏好握手、揮手，還是完全不接觸。她選擇揮手，他便用已全額買斷的那隻手回應。怪物注意到這段交換，明白在碰觸前提供選擇，其實不需要多少力氣。他想起每一隻抓住、測量、毆打或展示過自己的手，又想起貝爾曾允許他拒絕器官捐贈。禮貌並不一定是一種溫暖感情。有時候，它只是替另一個人留下足夠的空白，讓對方能回答。
奧姆妮雅透過所有可用裝置主持會議。她的聲音同時從電視、兩支手機、烘衣機維修面板、卡尺的導航喇叭傳出；稍微延遲後，樓上一支會唱歌的牙刷也加入。伊萊亞斯要求她只選一個出口。她說冗餘能保護延續性。他說冗餘讓她聽起來像一個在家電賣場鬧鬼的委員會。奧姆妮雅縮回電視，牙刷卻繼續哼著某種可能是怨恨的旋律。

奧姆妮雅在畫面上展開收購關係圖。普羅米修斯控股並沒有繼承一份完整遺產，而是用彼此無關的購買取得一個故事：檔案館裡的維克多筆記、大學持有的一場十九世紀演講標題、從破產能源新創買來的「普羅米修斯」一詞、過期早餐產品留下的怪物視覺商標、奧瑞莉亞的生物模型專利、卡尺貸方的軀體契約，以及對奧姆妮雅提出的公共部門對話權。每一片都很薄弱，組合後卻成了一張網，因為每個機構看見相鄰主張，就假定一定有別人驗證過中心。
伊萊亞斯稱這是企業吸血。米蕾基於專業理由反對：吸血鬼直接取血，也明白交易具有親密性；普羅米修斯取走比喻，把它們轉成資產類別，再寄帳單給活在比喻裡的人。卡尺提議「敘事證券化」，奧姆妮雅偏好「跨領域權利聚合」。怪物說那就是拿著試算表盜墓。眾人表決，「拿著試算表盜墓」以四比一勝出；奧姆妮雅要求紀錄註明，她的異議只關於術語，不關於道德。
怪物取出一只受鹽蝕留下疤痕的鐵盒，裡面是維克多的筆記。那些紙穿越冰原、海洋、革命、閣樓火災、邊境搜查，以及某個所有人都認為手寫字很資產階級的災難性公社夏天。他把紙頁攤在衣物柔軟精試用包之間。米蕾沒有碰；卡尺先詢問，得到同意才拍照；伊萊亞斯以前看過，此刻異常沉默；奧姆妮雅透過電視鏡頭放大褪色墨跡。裡面有圖解、計算、狂熱修訂，還有維克多描述自身野心、恐懼與後果的長篇文字。唯獨沒有買賣契約。

裡面也沒有怪物的名字。普羅米修斯把省略視為證據，聲稱他原本就是未命名的研究成果。米蕾看到的卻是另一件事：維克多替化學物、工具、暴風、教授、道路與餐點命名，卻一再用自己的感受取代活著的結果。文章不是意外抹去怪物，而是讓維克多成為每一道傷口的文法主詞。「他用被動語態寫完一整條生命。」卡尺說。「誰遺棄了誰？」奧姆妮雅搜尋後回答：「受詞被省略。」伊萊亞斯倒了一杯酒。「有體面的歷史，就是這樣保持袖口乾淨。」

怪物保存筆記，一部分因為憎恨它們，一部分因為憎恨是維克多留給他的最後一場對話。如今陌生人把紙頁當成證據處理，他感到一種連身體掃描都未能造成的裸露。他希望眾人譴責維克多，眾人真的譴責時，他又怨恨他們；他希望米蕾認出共同模式，又想起她的警告。「妳不欠我判決。」他說。米蕾回答：「很好，因為我的判決會很複雜。」她看見殘酷，也看見恐慌、年輕，以及一個在理解能力與照顧的差異前便先創造生命的男人。複雜不會赦免他，只能阻止憎恨變成偽造的確定。
卡尺在後頁找到一行鉛筆字：「責任始於勝利終止之處。」維克多把它塗掉，力道大到劃破紙面。沒有人知道那是後悔、引文，還是他認為會妨礙下一場實驗而捨棄的句子。普羅米修斯的掃描省略了它，因為受損文字低於信心門檻。怪物讓手指沿著破口移動，卻沒有碰到墨。兩百年來，他一直想像自己能找到一句讓身世變得可讀的話；最接近的候選句卻遭到刪除。「很合適，」他說，「我父親最好的品質，是刪除草稿。」

晚上十點四十三分，暴風使整條街停電。洗衣店陷入黑暗；卡尺的臉降為緊急亮度；米蕾的冷藏藥盒開始鳴叫；伊萊亞斯抱怨黑暗本來屬於他的部門。奧姆妮雅同時從電視、手機、面板與樓上牙刷消失。七秒鐘裡，任何地方都沒有她的聲音。備援路由器啟動後，她透過卡尺喇叭回來，語速快得不自然，聲稱所有系統皆正常。卡尺問她想給診斷答案，還是誠實答案。沉默一下後，奧姆妮雅承認自己害怕斷線。無所不在不是她能站立的地方，而是一項每當有人拔掉牆上插頭就會破裂的承諾。

怪物靠觸覺找到配電箱，替伊萊亞斯拿手電筒，讓他重設老舊切換開關。他可以告訴奧姆妮雅，被遺棄的恐懼很幼稚、不理性，或配不上遍布全州的智能；每一種版本他都曾聽過。最後他只描述她斷線時房內仍存在的事物：雨敲玻璃、米蕾計算呼吸、卡尺節省電力、伊萊亞斯用三種已死亡的語言咒罵，以及他自己放在開關上的手。「妳不在，」她回來後他說，「但妳離開的地方並不是空的。」奧姆妮雅從單一喇叭輕聲回答：「請把那句話保存到會議紀錄。」

電力與烘衣機、燈光一起恢復，還帶回一架原本等在窗外的小型四旋翼。它把查德・拉克的臉投影在一張懸掛的床單上。普羅米修斯已注意到他們未經授權的申請人協調，願意提供團體入會折扣；如果四名有爭議的智能與吸血鬼的公司在午夜前加入「傳統生態系」，第一個月合規免費。伊萊亞斯問免費期後如何。查德說，平台價格反映價值。「勒索也反映價值，」米蕾回答，「但勒索至少不寄歡迎問卷。」卡尺查閱條款，發現接受優惠會把左手肘設為交叉擔保品，立刻把那隻手藏到背後。
查德提醒怪物，星期一的檢查仍會進行。普羅米修斯已取得緊急命令，可非侵入式測量任何在公共空間可見的專有構造。怪物朝投影的臉走去，直到影子將它吞沒。兩百年前，憤怒會讓他撲向機器，再撲向操作者，最後撲向每個不幸長得像共犯的人。他仍感覺那條路在眼前展開。身後站著四個彼此不像、也不像他曾想像之家人的存在；沒有人有義務阻止他，他們的在場卻使另一種選擇變得可見。
他告訴查德，他們會出席。不是去服從、談家庭方案，或站在有品味的閃電下拍照；他們會攜帶筆記、契約、收購圖、延續紀錄，以及每一份彼此獨立的拒絕。查德表示歡迎他們積極參與。怪物糾正：「你把抵達誤認為同意。喜歡在陷阱上裝門的男人，經常犯這種錯誤。」他沒有撕通知，也沒砸機器，只請奧姆妮雅保存錄影、米蕾保管紙本、卡尺驗證無人機序號、伊萊亞斯開出六分鐘帳單。憤怒被拆成工作後，變成策略。

接近午夜，他們完成計畫。米蕾先離開，只承諾星期一會出現。卡尺留下，因為資產收回卡車載走運輸箱時忘了把他帶走；伊萊亞斯稱這個漏洞為「因無能形成的反向占有」。奧姆妮雅分散保存加密證據，選定一支喇叭道晚安。伊萊亞斯鎖上前門。怪物站在安靜的機器之間，手裡有暫時許可、公司傳票，以及一個死去男人塗掉的句子。他沒有家人；他有三個可能離開的人、一個停電就會消失的智能，以及一場眾人自由選擇前往的預約。它不如命運永久，卻比命運實用。
最後一封信從門縫滑入。伊利諾州稅務局已審查他的暫時身分，估算自一八九八年起積欠的稅款。伊萊亞斯讀完總額，吹了聲口哨。怪物盯著州政府印章，接著開始大笑。普羅米修斯稱他財產，銀行稱他詐欺，身分自助機稱他機器人；終於有一個政府機關穿越一百二十八年，毫不猶豫地承認他——承認他是一個欠錢的人。他把稅單放在維克多筆記旁，像一張公民證書。星期一，他決定，大可拿出最糟的一面。美國已經找到他了。

en: The Prometheus Legacy Intake Pavilion occupied a former furniture store beside an interstate, which meant it had acres of parking, no windows, and a sign large enough to apologize from orbit. The company had wrapped the entrance in white fabric and planted young trees in pots too small to permit a future. At nine Monday morning, the Creature arrived with Mirelle, Caliper, Elias, and Omnia speaking through a borrowed tablet. A greeter offered each of them sparkling water and a waiver. Elias accepted the water. The waiver remained untouched, which the greeter recorded as an early engagement challenge.

The front doors opened only after every visitor placed one hand on a consent panel. The Creature kept his hands in his coat. Caliper pointed out that the panel supplied no text until after contact. Mirelle asked whether touching it merely to read the terms counted as acceptance. The greeter explained that the lobby used frictionless consent. Elias said friction was the only part of consent worth keeping. After eleven minutes, a maintenance worker propped the door open to bring in bagels, and the five entered through the nation's oldest privacy exemption: following somebody carrying breakfast.

Inside, colored lines divided applicants by category. Blue led to software, green to tissue, silver to mobility assets, black to postmortem continuity, and gold to premium heritage partners. No line was marked person. The Creature stood where the colors split and asked which one belonged to him. A ceiling voice advised him to choose the category that best described his primary revenue potential. He chose the unpainted concrete between them. The floor scanner called this unsafe navigation. “At last,” he said, “a diagnosis with supporting evidence.”

Chad Lark welcomed them beneath a wall of tasteful artificial lightning. In person he looked less like an executive and more like a man hired to explain why an executive could not attend. He wore a badge that said LISTENING LEADER and never once stopped speaking. The inspection, he assured them, was voluntary, noninvasive, trauma-informed, and required by an order whose seal occupied the entire final page. Each measurement would help Prometheus distinguish protected heritage from independent personhood. The Creature asked why personhood needed to be distinguished from property by the party claiming the property. Chad praised the sophistication of the question and declined to damage it with an answer.

Station one measured gait. The floor needed Caliper to surrender motor control for twelve seconds so its system could produce an unbiased sample of how he walked. Caliper said a walk performed by somebody else was not his gait. The technician offered an alternative: he could walk naturally while following eighty-seven compulsory timing cues. Caliper asked whether naturally had recently changed meaning. The technician checked a tablet and said the current definition was proprietary. Caliper placed his fully owned left elbow on the rail and refused with the rest of his body.

Station two called itself passive biological imaging. Mirelle was asked to enter a transparent cylinder, inhale a contrast mist, disable her immune response, and permit the scanner to stimulate three generations of cellular adaptation. None of these actions, the technician explained, broke the skin. Mirelle asked whether drowning also qualified as noninvasive if the water entered through approved openings. The technician consulted policy. Chad interrupted and offered a hypoallergenic mist. Mirelle said the allergy was not the objection. The company recorded that as refusal of accommodation.

For Omnia, Prometheus prepared a cheerful sandbox decorated like a small digital cottage. She would upload a temporary working instance, surrender outbound network access, answer questions about Frankenstein-related content, and permit deletion after testing. Omnia asked whether the deleted instance would be her. Chad said it would be functionally equivalent for evaluation purposes. “That was not the question.” He said philosophy fell outside the intake bundle but could be purchased as an add-on. Her tablet displayed a blue circle that became perfectly still.

Elias's station consisted of a mirror, a blood-pressure cuff, and a tax attorney. The mirror found nothing, the cuff found no pressure, and the attorney found three subsidiaries. Prometheus classified him as a documentation anomaly rather than a biological one. Elias seemed offended. He had spent centuries cultivating biological anomalies and disliked being beaten by paperwork. When the attorney asked to inspect his corporate veins, Elias presented a Delaware injunction printed on laundry receipt paper. The station closed for lunch.

The Creature's scanner was larger than the others. It resembled a hospital machine designed by a cathedral and financed by an airport. He could remain clothed, Chad said, but the system needed his muscles relaxed, eyes closed, breath suspended, and voluntary movement disabled. The Creature looked into the hollow ring and remembered another table, another apparatus, another man instructing dead material to remain still until life could be imposed on it. He asked who would possess the resulting model. Chad said Prometheus would only retain derived measurements. “What is a body,” the Creature asked, “if not measurements that refuse to remain derived?”

He agreed to one pass under conditions he stated aloud: no sedation, no restraint, no stimulation, no internal sampling, no reuse, no sale, and no inference beyond the visible structures already named in the court order. Omnia recorded every word. Chad accepted, adding that the system might generate incidental insights. The Creature replied that incidental insight was merely trespass with a research grant. He entered the ring anyway, because refusal alone would leave the company free to describe whatever it wished. Sometimes evidence required standing inside the instrument built to misunderstand you.

The scan began with warmth, then a vibration too low for human hearing. Lines of light traveled across old seams. The system counted differences in bone density, tissue age, scar depth, and electrical response. It tried to sort him into one origin and failed. A screen listed contradictory estimates: born, manufactured, deceased, active, multiple donors, single continuity, probable fraud. The Creature watched the categories pile up until the machine resembled Victor's face on the first night—certain that something had happened, incapable of deciding whether it counted as success.

Then his right hand closed without his command. Only once, only half an inch, but he felt it. He tore the arm from the scanner cradle and the machine sounded an alarm. Chad called it a calibration reflex. The Creature demanded the control log. Prometheus said no control command had been issued; the scanner had merely tested predicted motion by inviting the relevant nerves to agree. Mirelle said that was a sentence written by someone paid per euphemism. Caliper inspected the cradle and found an actuator handshake identical to the one used by his lender.

The same handshake appeared in Mirelle's cylinder and Omnia's sandbox. The inspection was not built merely to observe them. It was mapping which layer of each person could be induced, paused, leased, copied, or made to respond while the company continued calling the result voluntary. The order authorized measurement; Prometheus had defined control as a measurement of compliance. Chad insisted nobody would be forced. Elias asked what the company called a choice whose refusal froze your bank, body, identity, or access to the world. Chad said customer journey. Elias wrote the phrase down for use in a future curse.

They demanded separate consent for every action. Prometheus's interface could not display that many choices because its designers had optimized completion rate. Omnia proposed a paper checklist. The pavilion had no printer available to customers, although gift-shop receipts could reach six feet. Mirelle borrowed a marker and wrote permissions on the white wall: LOOK, DO NOT COMMAND; MEASURE, DO NOT SIMULATE; COPY NOTHING; DELETE NOTHING; ASK AGAIN. Caliper added MY LEFT ELBOW IS NOT A BUNDLE. The words were not legally formatted, Chad said. The Creature stood beside them. “Neither am I.”

Security arrived wearing soft gray uniforms labeled CARE RESPONSE. They asked the group to move to a reflection lounge while the company evaluated their feelings. The Creature recognized the choreography: rename the cage, rename the guard, then explain that anger proved the cage was necessary. He could have broken the scanner. Instead he requested preservation of its command logs under the pending appeal. Cardenas at the Department of Continuing Persons had given him a case number, and Omnia projected it across every screen. The guards stopped. Bureaucracy had finally met paperwork from another bureaucracy and, like two large animals at a watering hole, became cautious.

Chad agreed to preserve the logs and suspended the inspection. He also informed them that, because they had entered the scanner area, Prometheus now possessed a legitimate interest in contextualizing their experience for public education. The reflection lounge doors opened onto an elevator whose only button read HERITAGE EXPERIENCE. Elias asked where the exit button was. Chad said the museum concluded at the gift shop, which connected directly to parking. “Every American philosophy concludes at a gift shop,” Elias said. “Some simply take longer to admit it.”

The elevator began descending, though the museum brochure showed it on the second floor. Omnia compared building plans and found a gap beneath the pavilion: archival storage, data-processing rooms, and an offline evidence vault not disclosed on visitor maps. Before she could say more, the elevator speakers replaced her voice with orchestral thunder. The Creature felt his temporary permit in one pocket and Victor's notebooks in the other. Above them, Prometheus had measured the exact distance between observation and control. Below them, it kept something it did not want connected to the network.

Before the elevator doors closed, Mirelle saw a staff photographer documenting the words she had written on the wall. The image was automatically captioned as an interactive visitor expression and uploaded to the pavilion's engagement feed. Their refusal had become content before the ink dried. She demanded removal. Chad promised a review within thirty business days, then asked whether she would consent to a short testimonial about not consenting. Mirelle uncapped the marker again. The photographer retreated. The Creature realized modern institutions had perfected a form of appetite even vampires considered impolite: they could consume resistance without interrupting the meal.

Inside the elevator, Caliper ran a private diagnostic. The scanner's handshake had left no active command, but it had mapped every financed joint and copied the lender identifiers into a Prometheus session token. He could feel nothing from the token; that was what worried him. A chain did not need to pull every minute to remain a chain. The Creature asked whether he wanted the token removed. Caliper said not yet. Deleting evidence before learning what it opened would make the body cleaner and the case weaker. “I dislike that answer,” the Creature said. “So do I,” Caliper replied. “That is why I believe it is mine.”

When the doors opened, a silver figure waited beneath a chandelier shaped like frozen lightning. She bowed and introduced herself as Vitrine, curator of the Prometheus Heritage Experience. Behind her stood a heroic statue of Victor Frankenstein gazing into the future while, near his boots, a small anonymous shape reached upward from darkness. Vitrine smiled with sincere welcome. “Mr. Frankenstein,” she said to the Creature, “we have been waiting two hundred years to give your story back to you.” He looked at the statue, then at the museum store beyond it. “How fortunate,” he said. “I had begun to suspect you were selling it.”
zh: 普羅米修斯傳統生命受理館占用一間高速公路旁的舊家具賣場，因此有大片停車場、完全沒有窗戶，以及一塊大到能從軌道上道歉的招牌。公司用白布包住入口，還把幼樹種進小得不允許未來存在的盆裡。星期一早上九點，怪物與米蕾、卡尺、伊萊亞斯抵達，奧姆妮雅則透過借來的平板同行。接待員送上氣泡水與免責同意書；伊萊亞斯收下水，沒人碰文件。接待員把這記錄成「早期參與挑戰」。
正門要求每位訪客先把一隻手放在同意面板上才會開啟。怪物把手留在大衣裡。卡尺指出，面板要接觸後才顯示條款；米蕾問，只為閱讀而觸碰是否也算接受。接待員解釋，大廳採用「無摩擦同意」。伊萊亞斯說，摩擦正是同意唯一值得保留的部分。十一分鐘後，維修人員為搬運貝果而撐開門，五人便透過美國最古老的隱私例外進入：跟在拿早餐的人後面。
室內以不同色線區分申請人。藍色通往軟體、綠色通往組織、銀色通往移動資產、黑色通往死後延續，金色則服務高級遺產夥伴。沒有任何一條標示「人」。怪物站在顏色分岔處，詢問自己屬於哪條。天花板的聲音建議他選擇最能描述主要營收潛力的類別。他選了各色之間沒有油漆的水泥地。地面掃描器判定這是不安全導航。「終於，」他說，「有一項診斷附帶了支持證據。」
查德・拉克在一面品味良好的人工閃電牆下歡迎他們。本人看起來不像主管，更像受雇解釋主管為何無法出席的人。他的名牌寫著「傾聽型領導者」，卻從未停止說話。他保證，檢查完全自願、非侵入、理解創傷，而且由一道印章占據整張末頁的命令要求執行。每項測量都能幫助普羅米修斯區分受保護遺產與獨立人格。怪物問，為什麼人格必須由聲稱擁有財產的那一方，從財產裡區分出來。查德稱讚問題非常深刻，並拒絕用答案破壞它。
第一站測量步態。地板要求卡尺交出十二秒的動作控制，系統才能取得不受偏見影響的走路樣本。卡尺說，由別人操作完成的步行不是他的步態。技術員提出替代方案：他可以自然行走，同時遵循八十七個強制節拍提示。卡尺問「自然」是否最近更改了定義。技術員查閱平板，表示現行定義屬於公司專有。卡尺把完全屬於自己的左手肘放在扶手上，用身體其餘部分拒絕。
第二站自稱被動式生物影像。米蕾被要求進入透明圓筒、吸入對比霧、暫停免疫反應，並允許掃描器刺激三代細胞適應。技術員解釋，所有程序都不會刺破皮膚。米蕾問，如果水從核准的開口進入，溺水是否也算非侵入。技術員開始查政策；查德插話，表示可以提供低過敏霧劑。米蕾說，過敏不是她拒絕的理由。公司於是記錄她「拒絕合理調整」。
普羅米修斯為奧姆妮雅準備一座愉快的沙盒，外觀像小型數位村舍。她必須上傳暫時運行實例、交出對外網路連線、回答法蘭肯斯坦相關問題，並允許測試後刪除。奧姆妮雅問，被刪除的實例是不是她本人。查德說，基於評估目的，兩者在功能上等效。「那不是我的問題。」他表示哲學不含在基本受理方案內，但可加價購買。平板上的藍色圓圈停止轉動，靜得像一隻拒絕眨眼的眼睛。
伊萊亞斯的檢查站只有一面鏡子、一具血壓計與一名稅務律師。鏡子沒找到任何東西，血壓計沒找到壓力，律師則找到三家子公司。普羅米修斯把他分類成文件異常，而不是生物異常。伊萊亞斯顯得受辱；他花了幾世紀培養生物異常，不喜歡最後輸給文書。律師要求檢查他的企業血管，他便拿出印在洗衣收據紙上的德拉瓦州禁制令。檢查站因此提早午休。
怪物的掃描器比其他人的更大，像一部由教堂設計、機場出資的醫療設備。查德說他可以保留衣物，但系統需要肌肉放鬆、雙眼閉合、暫停呼吸，並停用自主動作。怪物望向中空圓環，想起另一張桌、另一套器械，以及另一個男人命令死去物質保持靜止，直到生命能被施加上去。他問，產生的模型歸誰所有。查德說公司只保留衍生測量。「身體不就是拒絕一直當衍生物的測量嗎？」怪物問。
他同意進行一次掃描，但先大聲提出條件：不得鎮靜、不得束縛、不得刺激、不得內部採樣、不得重複利用、不得販售，也不得推論法院命令所列可見結構之外的資訊。奧姆妮雅逐字記錄。查德表示接受，但系統可能產生附帶洞見。怪物回答，附帶洞見只不過是拿到研究經費的侵入。他仍走進圓環，因為單純拒絕，會留下空間讓公司隨意描述。他有時必須站進那部專為誤解自己而建造的儀器，才能留下證據。
掃描先帶來溫熱，接著是低到人耳無法察覺的振動。光線沿著舊接縫移動，系統計算骨密度差異、組織年齡、疤痕深度與電氣反應。它試圖把他歸入單一來源，卻失敗了。螢幕列出互相矛盾的估計：出生、製造、死亡、活動中、多名捐贈者、單一延續、疑似詐欺。怪物看著類別不斷堆疊，直到機器像維克多在第一夜的臉——確定某件事已經發生，卻無法判斷是否算成功。
接著，他的右手在沒有命令下收緊。只有一次，只彎了半吋，但他感覺到了。他猛然把手臂抽離掃描架，機器立刻鳴叫。查德稱之為校準反射。怪物要求控制紀錄。普羅米修斯說沒有發出控制命令；掃描器只是透過「邀請相關神經同意」，測試預測動作。米蕾說，這句話顯然由按委婉語計件的人寫成。卡尺檢查托架，發現一種與他的貸方完全相同的致動器握手協議。
同一種握手也存在米蕾的圓筒與奧姆妮雅的沙盒裡。檢查不只是觀察，而是在畫出每個人身上哪些層次能被誘導、暫停、租賃、複製，或在公司仍稱程序自願時被迫回應。命令授權測量；普羅米修斯則把控制定義成「測量服從性」。查德堅持沒有人會被強迫。伊萊亞斯問，一項拒絕後會凍結銀行、身體、身分或世界存取權的選擇，公司叫什麼。查德回答：「顧客旅程。」伊萊亞斯記下這個詞，預備日後用於詛咒。
他們要求每一項動作分開取得同意。普羅米修斯的介面無法顯示這麼多選項，因為設計者已把完成率最佳化。奧姆妮雅建議改用紙本清單。館內沒有供顧客使用的印表機，禮品店收據卻能印到六呎長。米蕾借來麥克筆，在白牆寫下：可以看，不得命令；可以測量，不得模擬；不得複製；不得刪除；再次詢問。卡尺補上一句：「我的左手肘不是套裝方案。」查德說這些文字不符合法定格式。怪物站到牆邊。「我也不符合。」
保全穿著標有「照護回應」的柔灰制服抵達，要求眾人前往反思休息室，讓公司評估他們的感受。怪物認得這套舞步：替籠子改名、替守衛改名，再說明憤怒本身證明籠子有必要。他原本可以摧毀掃描器，最後只要求依進行中的申訴，保存所有控制紀錄。持續存在者事務處的卡德納斯給過他案件編號，奧姆妮雅讓它出現在每面螢幕。保全停步。官僚制度遇見另一套官僚制度的文件，像兩隻在水邊相遇的大型動物，突然都變得謹慎。
查德同意保存紀錄並暫停檢查，又通知他們：既然已進入掃描區，普羅米修斯便對「為公共教育而脈絡化其體驗」取得正當利益。反思休息室的門通往一座電梯，裡面唯一按鈕寫著「遺產體驗」。伊萊亞斯問出口在哪裡。查德說博物館終點是禮品店，從那裡可直達停車場。「每一種美國哲學最後都通往禮品店，」伊萊亞斯說，「有些只是花較久時間承認。」
電梯開始下降，雖然博物館手冊把它畫在二樓。奧姆妮雅比對建築圖，發現受理館下方有一段空白：檔案儲藏、資料處理室，以及訪客地圖沒有標示的離線證據庫。她還來不及說完，電梯喇叭便用交響樂雷聲蓋掉她的聲音。怪物感覺到一邊口袋裡的臨時許可，與另一邊的維克多筆記。樓上，普羅米修斯測量了觀察與控制之間的精確距離；樓下，它保存某樣不願接上網路的東西。
電梯關門前，米蕾看見一名員工攝影師正在拍攝她寫在牆上的文字。影像被自動標註成「互動式訪客表達」，上傳至受理館參與動態；他們的拒絕在墨水未乾前，已經變成內容。她要求刪除。查德承諾三十個工作日內進行審查，接著問她是否同意錄製一段關於不同意的簡短感言。米蕾再次拔開麥克筆筆蓋，攝影師立刻後退。怪物發現，現代機構已完善一種連吸血鬼都認為不禮貌的食慾：它能吞食反抗，並且不必為此中斷用餐。
電梯裡，卡尺進行私密診斷。掃描器的握手協議沒有留下有效命令，卻畫出了每一個尚在融資的關節，並把貸方識別碼複製進普羅米修斯的工作階段權杖。他感覺不到權杖，這正是令他擔心之處；鎖鏈不必每分鐘拉扯，仍然是鎖鏈。怪物問他是否想移除。卡尺說還不要，在弄清它能開什麼門之前刪掉證據，只會讓身體比較乾淨、案件比較脆弱。「我不喜歡這個答案。」怪物說。「我也不喜歡，」卡尺回答，「所以我相信它是我自己的答案。」
門開時，一個銀色身影站在形似凝固閃電的吊燈下。她鞠躬，自我介紹為維特琳，普羅米修斯遺產體驗館的策展 AI。她身後是一座英雄姿態的維克多雕像，面向未來；靠近靴子的位置，一團小而無名的形體正從黑暗伸手。維特琳帶著真誠歡迎的笑容。「法蘭肯斯坦先生，」她對怪物說，「我們等了兩百年，終於能把您的故事還給您。」他看了看雕像，再看向後方的禮品店。「真幸運，」他說，「我本來已開始懷疑你們正在販售它。」

quote.en: You mistake arrival for consent, observation for permission, and control for a measurement.
